name: GraphXSource
what_it_does: A 40-year-old apparel-decoration prepress and art services bureau in Dallas, TX. Core services: embroidery digitizing, high-end screen-print color separations, vector/production art recreation, and image mapping — plus two newer motions: (1) 'Dedicated Art Staffing', month-subscription remote FTEs embedded in a customer's team (published plans: Pixel Pro $2,449/mo graphic designer, Halftone Hero $3,249/mo separations+creative, Hybrid Hotshots $3,249/mo designer+data entry, Data Driver $2,449/mo order processing, Answer Agent $2,449/mo customer-service rep — note 'Answer Agent' is a human, not an AI agent), and (2) GraphXServer.io, a workflow-automation/order-management platform for artwork intake, approval and asset organization. Current positioning is 'your first AI-supported prepress department' and 'Human Expertise + API Efficiency'. Site claims 99.7% accuracy, 24-hour turnaround, 50% lower prepress labor cost. Founded 1984 as a domestic embroidery digitizing operation; opened offshore delivery in the late 1990s. Slite's case study says five countries (Honduras, US, El Salvador, Thailand, India) with a newer in-house dev team in Honduras; the current site says six offices in six countries. Also runs GraphX Academy, an Adobe Creative Suite training/certification arm aimed at Central America.
category: Creative BPO / art-and-prepress outsourcing and staffing for the apparel decoration and promotional-products industry (services business with an automation layer, not a software vendor)
stage: Bootstrapped / family-owned, 4 generations, no institutional capital found. Tracxn (2025) states no funding raised.
funding: None found. Tracxn: 'Graphx Source has not raised any funding yet.' ZoomInfo-style third-party revenue estimate of ~$4.5M appeared in search results but is unverified and looks low relative to a 900-1,000 person headcount — do not rely on it.
headcount_estimate: 501-1,000 (LinkedIn company page band). Own site says '1,000+ staff, 6 offices, 6 countries'; a DTF Expo exhibitor listing says '900+ staff'. Treat 700-1,000 as the honest range. Note this is a labor-heavy production workforce, not a tech headcount — the internal dev team is small and recently formed in Honduras.
yc_or_accelerator: None
sells_to: B2B SMB primarily — screen print and embroidery shops, decorators, promotional-products distributors — with some larger apparel brands and industry accounts. Sold as a service subscription/per-job, US-based account leads over offshore production staff.
how_they_use_agents: No agentic AI in the product. Their 'AI' is workflow automation, scripting and image-processing applied to artwork prep, marketed as an AI-supported prepress department. Where AI genuinely shows up is as an internal consumer: they replaced Obsidian (with Git-plugin sync workarounds) and evaluated Notion, landing on Slite, and the retrieval feature 'Ask AI' is the headline value. Christian Rivera, Director of App Development: 'Ask AI is very useful because people don't always want to read long SOPs or well-documented APIs. Our image mapping team especially loves it — their documents have tons of images and steps.' He describes the whole system as 'your notebook... but with a personal assistant you can talk to.' They also run week-long UI/UX design sprints with live simultaneous note-taking, and use Airtable, Figma and Gmail alongside.
why_they_need_memory: Scale + distribution + churn. Roughly 900-1,000 production staff across five to six countries and time zones, doing highly proceduralized creative work (digitizing, separations, image mapping) that is documented in long, image-dense SOPs. Onboarding offshore artists and keeping process knowledge consistent across Honduras/El Salvador/Thailand/India is the actual pain; the failure mode they named was unsynced personal notes in Obsidian. This is classic org-knowledge retrieval, not agent state — they buy 'company brain' for humans, and would only need durable agent memory if GraphXServer.io grew an agent that had to know a client's brand rules, artwork history and approval preferences across jobs.

name: TSN Lab
what_it_does: Korean deep-tech company building deterministic real-time networking, vertically integrated 'from semiconductor IP to application'. Product lines: Silicon Logic IP cores (TSN IP verified with Germany's Fraunhofer IPMS, industrial RISC-V CPU IP with ASIL-D path, Low Latency MAC IP, MACsec controller IP up to 10Gbps); hardware (TSN PCIe NIC for PCs/servers supporting 802.1AS/Qav/Qbv, the world-first TSN HAT for Raspberry Pi 5, 10BASE-T1S HATs and media converters); software (TSN SDK and 10BASE-T1S SDK for Zephyr RTOS and FreeRTOS, Packetvisor — a Rust/Linux-XDP high-speed packet I/O framework, Ceno service-chaining platform, TickLE micro-ROS middleware for 10BASE-T1S); and professional services including RTOS porting, TSN integration and AI-model optimization for sensors. Target verticals: automotive, rail, aerospace, defense, robotics and smart factories. Spun out of a TSN project at the Korea Railroad Research Institute. Radically flat and remote-first: no titles, only roles; four-day week with no pay cut; 20 days leave plus 20 days 'workcation'; a worker-director on the board; Scrum company-wide.
category: Deep tech — time-sensitive networking / deterministic Ethernet semiconductors, RTOS and embedded networking (edge infrastructure for autonomous vehicles and factory automation)
stage: Seed / pre-Series A deep tech, with heavy Korean government R&D funding as a revenue source
funding: Investment from Hanyang Holdings (Hanyang University's technology holding company) reported around May-July 2023 at a KRW 5 billion (~USD 3.7-3.9M) company valuation; selected for Korea's Deep Tech TIPS program (government matching for deep-tech startups). Exact round size was not disclosed in the sources I could reach — the KRW 5bn figure is a valuation, not the amount raised, and I could not confirm the check size. Substantial non-dilutive revenue from state R&D contracts: Korea Aerospace Research Institute, Korea Railroad Research Institute, ETRI and KETI awards (2024-2025), a 42dot (Hyundai) next-gen automotive RTOS development and certification contract (Oct 2024), and selection for the SMEs and Startups Ministry 'Global Cooperative R&D' program (Sept 2025).
headcount_estimate: ~16-17. Slite's case study states 16 employees working remotely; Korean startup databases list ~17. Hiring FPGA, hardware-board and embedded developers as of the current careers page.
yc_or_accelerator: Deep Tech TIPS (Korean government/private matching accelerator program), 2023. No YC.
founded_year: 2021 (incorporated 20 January 2021)
sells_to: B2B enterprise, OEMs and developers. IP cores to chip/system OEMs (TSN IP sold Korea-only), NICs/HATs and SDKs to embedded developers and research institutes, plus consulting/system integration. Government research institutes and universities are a major channel. Also opened a Naver Smart Store (Mar 2026) for direct dev-board sales.
how_they_use_agents: Effectively none in the product. Their AI story is adjacent, not agentic: 'real-time AI' and 'Sensor AI' as a stated core competency, AI model optimization for sensors as a professional service, and positioning TSN as the network substrate for the 'physical AI' era (they ran a July 2026 demo event on exactly that framing). Where AI actually touches them day to day is as a buyer: a 16-person fully remote team that ran on ClickUp, evaluated Notion/Jira/Confluence, and moved to Slite in 2023 for a tree-structured wiki with role-based access — meeting notes, VPN and tool-setup guides, team folders, technical wikis — with AI search over it. Their AI/technical screening stage in hiring is the only other AI mention.
why_they_need_memory: Small, senior, fully remote and deliberately hierarchy-free — which means written documentation is the only coordination mechanism. Their stated pain with ClickUp was poor real-time sync during collaborative editing and unreliable document history, i.e. they lost knowledge. The content is dense embedded/hardware documentation (RTOS porting notes, board bring-up, infra setup) where an answer must be traceable and correct. This is a company-brain/knowledge-retrieval buyer, not an agent-memory buyer: nothing in their stack runs an LLM agent that needs persistent state. Note their headcount and price sensitivity make them a small-ACV logo.

name: Filmustage
what_it_does: AI pre-production platform for film and TV: upload a locked script and it auto-tags cast, props, wardrobe, locations, sets and VFX in any language, then generates a shooting schedule/stripboard, budget templates, call sheets, storyboards, VFX breakdowns and script analysis/synopsis — one connected system from script to first shooting day. Claims 45,000+ filmmakers (was 15,000 registrations at the Aug 2024 seed announcement), covering features, series, shorts, vertical drama and podcasts. Pricing: Free (partial AI breakdown, 20% of scenes, 1 project); Director's Cut $55/mo or $660/yr with a coin-based AI credit system, unlimited projects; Enterprise custom for studios; academic tier. Trust posture is a selling point: SOC 2 Type II, TPN Blue Shield member, US-hosted script storage, and an explicit 'we do not use your data for training neural networks.' Hall of Fame cites productions including Netflix's The Gentlemen, Universal's Nobody 2, and Apple TV+'s Masters of the Air — read these as credits where the tool was used, not necessarily as enterprise contracts. Advised by former WarnerMedia VP Byron Saltysiak, Crafty Apes co-founder Chris LeDoux, and ex-Warner Bros. executive Barry Loudis, plus a former Final Draft SVP.
category: AI-native vertical SaaS — film/TV production management (script breakdown, scheduling, budgeting); media & entertainment tech
stage: Seed (post-seed, likely raising or approaching Series A given 2020 founding and ~20 headcount)
funding: Approximately $2.11M total across 3 rounds per Tracxn (one aggregator cited ~$3.1M — sources conflict, so treat the total as roughly $2-3M, not precise). Known rounds: a ~$550K round from Flyer One Ventures, Geek Ventures, Vesna Capital and Imaguru; and a $1.5M seed announced 27 August 2024, led by Raw Ventures with Geek Ventures participating. Other investors named across databases: New York Angels, GAMEGROOVE Capital, TA Ventures. Stated use of the seed: Tier-1 B2B client acquisition, AI budget estimation, AI storyboards, marketplace and Omniverse integrations. Business Insider covered the seed pitch deck.
headcount_estimate: ~17-20. LinkedIn shows the 11-50 band with 17 employee profiles; Tracxn 18; Getlatka 19; PitchBook 20.
yc_or_accelerator: No YC. Imaguru (Minsk-founded accelerator and fund) is an investor; I could not confirm whether they went through an Imaguru program batch versus taking a check.
founded_year: 2020 (first Product Hunt launch January 2020; company incorporated in Delaware, HQ listed as Wilmington, DE — the team itself is distributed across countries and time zones and the founders appear to be from the CIS/Eastern European ecosystem)
sells_to: Prosumer and B2B SMB with an enterprise studio motion. Individual filmmakers, 1st ADs, line producers and production companies self-serve on the $55/mo tier; studios and production companies buy Enterprise with granular department permissions, tailored contracts and 24/7 support. Academic tier for film schools.
how_they_use_agents: This is the one genuine agent company of the three. They ship an 'AI Production Agent' branded 'AI Dude' — marketed as an industry first, voice-controlled, and explicitly framed as an agent that executes rather than only analyzes. It reads the script, updates breakdowns, directly edits the stripboard, surfaces and resolves schedule conflicts, detects production risks, optimizes workload across shooting days, generates call sheets, and applies bulk structured changes across the project with a preview-before-approval step. Their own blog (March 2026, 'How AI Agents Are Rewiring Film Pre-Production') describes a single agent operating across the whole project. The agent shipped roughly 2025-2026, well after the 2024 seed. Separately, as a buyer, they consolidated Linear, Trello, Discord, Miro and scattered docs into Slite in 2022 as an internal knowledge base organized by area owner (Marketing, Product, SEO).
why_they_need_memory: Strongest real agent-memory case of the three. A film production is a long-lived, constantly-revised object — script revisions (with colored revision passes), breakdown tags, stripboard order, budget lines, call sheets — and an agent that 'executes structured changes across projects' has to hold that state across sessions, across a whole department team, and across weeks of revisions, or it will re-tag and re-break things it already decided. Add per-production conventions (how this AD names locations, which props are already tracked, which scenes are locked) and you need durable per-project and per-org memory, not just a context window. Their SOC 2 Type II posture and their public no-training-on-customer-data promise mean any memory layer has to be strictly tenant-isolated and non-training — a real constraint on which vendor they can buy. Caveat for targeting: at ~$2-3M raised and ~20 people, budget is small; the internal need (a distributed team's knowledge base) is what Slite actually sold them, and is separate from the product-side agent-memory need.

name: OneUp Sales
what_it_does: Sales and recruitment performance-management SaaS — a "performance layer" that pulls data out of ATS/CRMs (Bullhorn, JobAdder, Vincere), diallers/VoIP and timesheet systems and turns it into live dashboards, TV wallboards, leaderboards, gamified competitions, targets, scheduled reports and triggered alerts (email, MS Teams). A newer 'Coach' module runs structured 1:1s off live KPI data with carried-forward action items and PDF export for HR. Claims 350-400+ client agencies, 8,500+ active users, 45+ countries, and '+43% more placements'. Pricing is quote-only, banded by team size (<5 to 100+ recruiters).
category: vertical SaaS — sales performance management / RecTech analytics + gamification (not an AI company)
stage: Series A
funding: ~$6M total, per the company's own about-us timeline: $200K first round (2017), $3M Series A (2023), and "$6M in funding later" as of 2025. Investors not named on the site; Crunchbase returned 403 so this is unverified against a third-party database.
headcount_estimate: ~30-35. LinkedIn company page shows 30 employees; the Slite case study says "35+ people working remotely around the globe" (fully distributed, UK-registered).
yc_or_accelerator: unknown — no YC or accelerator affiliation found
founded_year: 2015 (first paying customer 2016); founded by Derry Holt (CEO) and James Heath (founding engineer)
sells_to: B2B SMB to lower mid-market — recruitment agencies primarily, plus sales teams; buyer is the agency owner / rec leader / sales ops, self-serve-ish demo motion with banded pricing from <5 to 100+ recruiters
how_they_use_agents: Very little. The only AI in the product is "AI Manager Briefings" inside the Coach module — AI-generated pre-1:1 summaries of a rep's performance, progress and recommended talking points. Everything else marketed as 'automation' is rule-based: scheduled leaderboard resets, KPI recaps, threshold-triggered alerts to Teams/email/TV screens. No autonomous agents, no agent framework, no AI in the pricing page or plan tiers. AI is a 2024-25 bolt-on to a 2015 data-and-gamification product.
why_they_need_memory: Their documented need is internal, not product: a 35-person fully-remote team that lost institutional knowledge in Confluence, with Head of Product Alex Wiley acting as self-appointed "documentation evangelist" and rebuilding docs on the Divio four-quadrant model (references / explanations / tutorials / how-tos) for onboarding and async Q&A. They bought a shared-knowledge wiki for onboarding and remote coordination — the classic 'company brain' internal-KM buyer, not an agent-memory infra buyer. A secondary latent need: the AI briefings would benefit from longitudinal per-rep coaching history, which is currently just rows in their own product DB.

name: Huli (HuliLabs / HuliHealth)
what_it_does: Latin American healthcare technology group building an integrated stack across the region's fragmented health system. Four products: HuliPractice (all-in-one practice management — scheduling, EMR, e-prescriptions, invoicing, automated reminders; certified to Mexican NOM-004/NOM-024 standards, HIPAA-compliant, on AWS); HuliVida (patient-controlled personal health record); HuliHealth (consumer marketplace to find and book verified doctors/dentists by specialty, price, availability); and MediCupón (digital coupon and sampling platform for pharma). Reported scale: 13,000+ healthcare providers, 400+ hospitals/medical centers, 3,000+ pharmacies, 35M+ appointments, 8 countries. Offices in Mexico and Costa Rica; commercial ops in Panama, Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Dominican Republic.
category: healthcare SaaS / LatAm health tech — EMR + practice management, plus a consumer booking marketplace and a pharma-monetization layer
stage: Pre-Series A (as labeled by the company)
funding: ~$7.5M disclosed, per the company's own site: US$2M round in 2019 led by Carao Ventures, and a US$5.5M Pre-Series A in 2023 led by Intoku Health with Carao Ventures. Crunchbase returned 403 so these figures are company-stated and not third-party verified.
headcount_estimate: ~60+ at the time of the Slite case study ("60+ team across Central America", six departments). Current size uncertain: the only LinkedIn page I could load is the HuliHealth showcase page, which shows the 11-50 band and does not represent the whole group. Treat current headcount as unknown; likely 50-150.
yc_or_accelerator: No YC. LinkedIn notes it won the Intel Costa Rica Challenge as an innovative idea; lead investor Carao Ventures is a Costa Rican seed fund/venture-builder, which is the closest thing to an accelerator link.
founded_year: 2012 per the company's own site ("founded 2012 in Costa Rica"); the Slite case study says 2013. Both figures are in circulation — the discrepancy is unresolved.
sells_to: Mixed B2B: SMB core (individual physicians, specialists, small and mid-size clinics buying HuliPractice seats, priced in MXN) plus enterprise/institutional (hospital networks, pharma companies, pharmacies, labs, insurers buying MediCupón and integrations). Also a B2C-facing marketplace, but consumers aren't the payer.
how_they_use_agents: Genuinely agent-shaped features, added recently and sold as paid add-ons on top of the EMR: (1) "Notas Clínicas IA" — an ambient AI scribe that listens live to the consultation, distinguishes speakers (patient, family, interruptions), and drafts the clinical note in medical language; sold at ~$400 MXN/month for 200 notes; marketed as not recording audio and not training on data without consent. (2) A WhatsApp "Bot Assistant" that autonomously handles appointment confirmations, reminders and rescheduling, priced per conversation (~30 conversations for $240 MXN, then ~$8 MXN each). These are the real agent surfaces — patient-facing conversational automation and clinical documentation — not a rules engine.
why_they_need_memory: Two distinct needs. Documented/internal: rapid growth created hard departmental silos across six departments each with its own docs, so the product team adopted Slite and the rest of the company followed — the buy was for cross-team discovery, de-duplicating overlapping processes (support vs. technical), and onboarding. Product-side (inferred, not stated): the AI scribe and the WhatsApp bot both need durable per-patient and per-practice context — prior visits, medication history, prescriber preferences, note style per physician — which is exactly agent-memory-shaped, though I found no evidence they buy any memory infrastructure today.

name: VanMoof
what_it_does: Dutch smart e-bike manufacturer and direct-to-consumer retailer. Designs connected city e-bikes (current line: S6, S6 Open, S5, A5) with integrated GPS tracking, automatic transmission, built-in anti-theft alarm and remote lock/unlock via a companion app, sold D2C with its own brand stores and service network in Amsterdam, New York, Berlin, Paris, London, Tokyo, Taipei and elsewhere. Also runs subscription services (Ride Pro, Theft-Proof/Peace of Mind) and B2B/employer leasing programs. This is a hardware and retail company — the odd one out in this buyer set.
category: consumer hardware / e-mobility (connected e-bikes) — not software, not AI
stage: Post-bankruptcy, acquired; now a subsidiary
funding: Raised $100M+ in venture funding before collapse — investors included Felix Capital, Balderton Capital, Hillhouse Capital, Norwest Venture Partners and TriplePoint Capital, with $40M raised in 2020 alone. Dutch entities declared bankrupt 17 July 2023 with roughly €143.8M owed to creditors, followed by insolvency filings in the UK (3 Aug), Germany (15 Aug) and a US Chapter 15 (19 Aug). Acquired 31 August 2023 by Lavoie, a subsidiary of McLaren Applied, for a reported "tens of millions" of pounds. No independent VC funding since.
headcount_estimate: ~191 today (LinkedIn, 51-200 band). Note a large discrepancy across sources for the peak: the Slite case study claims "1,000+ employees, grew by 400 people in one year" (which would include global retail and service staff at the 2021-22 peak), while Wikipedia cites 130 employees. The 1,000+ figure is Slite marketing copy and should not be treated as verified.
yc_or_accelerator: none
founded_year: 2009 (May), by brothers Taco Carlier and Ties Carlier, Amsterdam
sells_to: Primarily B2C / prosumer — premium D2C e-bikes at consumer price points, sold through own stores and web; secondary B2B channel via employer and leasing programs (Leasing Direct, Employee/Employer leasing, Become a Partner).
how_they_use_agents: None found. The connected-bike app provides GPS location, anti-theft alarm and remote lock, ride stats and firmware/service functions — telemetry and remote control, not AI. No AI agent, assistant, or LLM feature appears anywhere on the site, sitemap or app page. Their relationship to this category is purely as an internal-tooling buyer.
why_they_need_memory: Entirely internal and historical. During hypergrowth (the Slite case study cites +400 people in a year across a globally distributed org), knowledge lived in five separate tools and in a handful of individuals' heads, and new hires waited on documentation. Digital Manager Martijn Hazelaar consolidated onto one wiki with Slack integration and Google SSO, hitting ~70% active usage in two months. This is a scaling-onboarding pain, not an agent-memory need — and the case study predates the AI-agent era. Given the 2023 bankruptcy and much smaller current org, the original driver no longer applies.

name: Upvest
what_it_does: B2B investment infrastructure for European financial institutions. Sells a cloud-native, event-driven Investment API that bundles brokerage, settlement and custody behind one integration, so banks and fintechs can launch investing products without building or licensing the back end. Coverage: 100,000+ instruments (stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, bonds, securitised derivatives), fractional investing from EUR 1, automated savings plans, multi-asset portfolio management. Claims 99%+ automation of middle- and back-office processes (order lifecycle, reconciliation, regulatory reporting). Regulated: BaFin (Germany) and FCA (UK), ISO/IEC 27001. 30+ institutional clients including Revolut, N26, DKB, Santander's Openbank, Raisin, Webull, Zopa, plus 2026 partnerships with SumUp, Qonto, Satispay, Plum, CMC Markets, growney. 2M+ end users, 100M+ orders/year across 20+ markets. Hubs in Berlin, London and Tallinn.
category: fintech / embedded investing infrastructure (investment API, brokerage-settlement-custody as a service)
stage: Growth / late-stage venture (post-Series C; raised again in March 2026)
funding: Roughly USD 300M+ raised in total across rounds. Confirmed sequence: ~USD 6M Series A (Dec 2020, Earlybird); ~USD 4.8M Series A extension (May 2021); USD 42M Series B (Jun 2022, led by Bessemer Venture Partners); ~USD 32M round (Oct 2023; 10X Capital, ABN AMRO Ventures, Bessemer); EUR 100M Series C (announced 12 Dec 2024, led by Hedosophia with Sapphire Ventures, BlackRock, Bessemer); USD 125M announced 17 Mar 2026 = USD 90M equity co-led by Sapphire Ventures and Tencent, plus a USD 35M debt facility, with existing investors Bessemer and BlackRock. A third-party report (Finance Magnates via TradingView) put the March 2026 valuation at ~EUR 640M; Upvest did not disclose a valuation itself, so treat that number as reported, not confirmed.
headcount_estimate: 280 (stated by Upvest in its own March 2026 funding announcement). Note: at the time of the Slite testimonial (March 2021) the company was far smaller — Slite's case study describes a startup with 15+ open roles.
yc_or_accelerator: None found. Not a YC company; VC-backed from Berlin (Earlybird seed lineage).
sells_to: B2B enterprise (banks, neobanks, brokers, wealth and pension managers) with a strong developer-facing surface — the product is literally an API, so engineering teams are the users even though procurement is enterprise.
how_they_use_agents:
Two distinct layers, and both are real rather than marketing veneer.

In the product: Upvest markets 'AI-ready DPM and advisory' and, in the March 2026 raise, said it is rolling out 'AI-supported investment engines' with real-time programmable execution APIs so institutions can 'build autonomous, hyper-personalised advisory services to everyday retail investors at scale.' CEO Martin Kassing framed the round as funding 'the new AI investment economy.' So the agent is the customer's robo-advisor, executing against Upvest rails.

Internally (documented in a May 2026 post at upvest.co/blog/building-with-ai authored by Sebastien Jeanquier, the same person who gave the Slite testimonial): Claude rolled out company-wide March 2026; a EUR 20,000 per-employee annual token budget to remove experimentation friction; ~80% of features shipped with AI assistance; GitHub Copilot, Gemini, n8n, NotebookLM, incident.io AI SRE, Datadog anomaly detection, Wiz agentic remediation; a self-organised Engineering AI Guild. Most relevant to this category: an internal 'Upvest AI Toolkit' of 30 specialist agents, 36 skills and 40 rules encoding company conventions, and an MCP Gateway — authenticated middleware behind Okta SSO — that exposes Linear, GitHub, Datadog, Wiz and Slite to AI tools. Human review is still mandatory for production. Hard constraint: GDPR data residency, no PII to non-EU AI providers.
why_they_need_memory: The best fit of the three by a wide margin, and effectively a proof case for the category. The 2021 Slite pain — 'knowledge was either at the team level... obviously we knew that was not going to scale' — has recurred at 280 people, and Upvest has now built the agent-memory layer itself: they describe the AI Toolkit explicitly as organisational memory ('one engineer's breakthrough on Tuesday becomes everyone's baseline by Friday'), and they have already wired their wiki into the MCP Gateway so agents read it. That means they are a buyer who has validated the need, built a homegrown v1, and would evaluate a vendor on whether it beats their own toolkit — not on whether the problem is real. Two concrete buying constraints: EU data residency (no PII to non-EU providers) is a hard gate, and access must flow through their existing Okta/MCP Gateway rather than a separate permissions model. Champion profile is unusual and useful: the CSO owns both the knowledge-base rollout and the AI adoption programme, so security review and enthusiasm sit in the same person.
sources: Google results citing upvest.co/blog/upvest-raises-100m-series-c (12 Dec 2024), financialit.net coverage of the EUR 100M Series C and the USD 42M Series B, startupintros.com funding-round listing, and TradingView/Finance Magnates on the ~EUR 640M reported valuation

name: Idea Informatica S.r.l.

Secondary products: OASI GWB, a web-based ERP for single-location retailers (notably consumer electronics), and six Android companion apps (Articoli, Statistiche, Inventario, Planning, Spunta, Rilevamento Prezzi) for in-store and field work. Based at Via Loredano Bizzarri 9, Bargellino, 40012 Calderara di Reno (Bologna), Emilia-Romagna. Legal identity confirmed: VAT/P.IVA 00604821207, chamber-of-commerce registration 10/07/1982.
category: legacy SMB / vertical ERP software vendor (Italian retail and distribution gestionale)
stage: Bootstrapped, privately held S.r.l. — no venture funding, 40+ years old
funding: unknown — no funding found and almost certainly none. A privately held Italian S.r.l. registered in 1982; no VC, PE or accelerator involvement located. Italian company-registry aggregators list revenue/balance-sheet filings but no investment rounds.
headcount_estimate: ~18 (grew from 11 to 18 during the Slite engagement, per the case study, with a stated target of 20). A third-party Italian registry aggregator estimated 6-9 employees, which appears stale or based on a different ATECO filing — I weight the case study higher but flag the discrepancy. LinkedIn page has only ~270 followers, consistent with a firm of well under 25 people.
yc_or_accelerator: None. Not applicable — a 1980s-founded family-scale Italian software firm.
founded_year: 1982 (chamber-of-commerce registration 10/07/1982; the company and the Slite case study both describe it as founded in the early 1980s)
sells_to: B2B SMB — independent Italian retailers, distributors, consumer-electronics chains, cooperatives and purchasing consortia.
how_they_use_agents: None found. This is an honest zero. Nothing on ideainf.it, in the OASI product pages, or in the Android app listings mentions AI, LLMs, copilots or agents; the only automation language on the site is 'automatismi e procedure' meaning scripted workflow automation in the ERP. A targeted search for Idea Informatica plus 'intelligenza artificiale' returned only generic Italian ERP-and-AI trend articles from unrelated vendors (NTS Informatica, Scao), not anything from this company. Their Slite usage is a document wiki for humans, with no agent or AI dimension described in the case study either.
why_they_need_memory: Weak fit for agent memory; strong fit for a plain human wiki. Their stated problem was generational and archival, not computational: a workforce spanning ages 20 to 60s, business-critical knowledge scattered across local servers and individual personal computers, and no shared base for onboarding. The signature quote is about a 67-year-old, 40-year-tenure employee converting from resistance to enthusiasm — an adoption-and-change-management story, not a retrieval-quality one. Their buying criterion was explicitly ease of use across mixed technical ability, which is why they chose Slite over Coda, Nuclino and Confluence. For a vendor selling agent memory or a 'company brain' with an LLM layer, this profile is a cautionary data point: it is the kind of logo that fills a wiki vendor's customer page but has no agents to give memory to, and would likely churn or never activate an AI tier. Note also the disambiguation risk below.
sources: Google results surfacing the LinkedIn company page ('piccola impresa attiva nel settore IT dall'inizio degli anni '80. Sviluppiamo gestionali ERP per cooperative, piattaforme logistiche'), ufficiocamerale.it (P.IVA 00604821207, registration 10/07/1982), registroaziende.it, reportaziende.it and impresaitalia.info company records

Disambiguation note: a DIFFERENT 'Idea Informatica Srl - In Liquidazione' exists, founded 01/03/1989 in Bassano del Grappa (Vicenza, Veneto), per fatturatoitalia.it. That is not this company. The Slite customer is the Bologna entity at ideainf.it.

name: Guindi & Associates
what_it_does: Montreal-based CPA / accounting and consulting firm, operating since 1981. Services: bookkeeping (built on Xero with Hubdoc), tax planning, compliance, payroll (via Wagepoint), and advisory/business strategy. Client segments as stated on their own site: active businesses, medical professionals and investment companies; the Slite case study adds family-owned businesses, larger organisations and high-net-worth individuals. Positions itself as unusually technology-forward for a small firm — 'on the bleeding edge of new technologies,' supporting 75+ best-in-class applications, Xero Platinum Partner and Wagepoint Gold Partner. Office at 5950 Chemin de la Cote-des-Neiges, Suite 400, Montreal, QC H3S 1Z6; phone +1 514-447-8335. Named practitioners include Allan Guindi (CPA, CA) and Edmond Guindi (CPA). The firm also runs an offshore team in Morocco.
category: professional services — independent accounting/CPA and advisory firm (not a software company)
stage: Bootstrapped, owner-operated partnership — no outside capital
funding: unknown / not applicable. A 45-year-old private accounting practice; no funding rounds exist or would be expected.
headcount_estimate: ~25. Their own site states 25 team members; the Slite case study says they grew from 7 to approximately 25, including a team of 5 established in Morocco.
yc_or_accelerator: None. Not applicable.
sells_to: B2B SMB plus prosumer/individual — owner-managed and family businesses, medical professionals, investment holding companies, and high-net-worth private clients.
how_they_use_agents: None confirmed, and I found no evidence of any AI or agent product or workflow. Their entire technology narrative is app-stack automation rather than agents: Xero plus Hubdoc for bookkeeping data capture, Wagepoint for payroll, and a claimed 75+ supported applications. The Slite case study contains no AI or 'Ask Slite' mention specific to their implementation — the described use is a structured human knowledge base organised by function (bookkeeping, payroll, year-end) plus onboarding spaces. The only automation-shaped claim is that ~50% of team questions are now self-served from the knowledge base rather than asked of a colleague, which is deflection by search, not by agent.
why_they_need_memory: Their pain is procedural-knowledge cost, quantified in labour hours rather than model quality. Stated drivers: institutional knowledge living in employees' heads; repeated one-on-one training cycles as the firm tripled from 7 to 25; and, decisively, an offshore Morocco team of 5 that had to be trained in Canadian accounting practice at a distance. Claimed returns are ~10 hours of one-on-one training saved per new hire and ~50% of internal queries self-served, with the COO's compounding argument — 'even if you save just 10 minutes per person per day, when you multiply that across 25 people every single day, it compounds.' This is the archetypal 'ask the company brain' buyer: they want an authoritative, queryable SOP layer for humans, and the ROI story is headcount-hours, not agent accuracy. For an agent-memory vendor they are a plausible buyer of an AI answer layer over documented procedures, but there is no agent in their stack today to give memory to, and no engineering function to integrate one. Buying is a single-decision-maker motion — the COO, David Potofsky, evidently owns it outright.
sources: Google Business Profile / local listing confirming Guindi & Associates, Accountant, 5950 Chem. de la Cote-des-Neiges #400, Montreal QC H3S 1Z6, +1 514-447-8335, 5.0 rating over 14 reviews
LinkedIn profile of Allan Guindi, CPA CA, Guindi & Associates (Oct 2015-present); Pages Jaunes / Canada411 listings for Allan Guindi CPA and Edmond Guindi CPA at the same address

name: Karbon
what_it_does: Cloud practice-management platform for accounting and bookkeeping firms. It unifies workflow automation, job/project management, a shared email inbox and client-communication triage, a client portal, document management and eSignature, time tracking, budgets, billing/payments, and reporting into one system of record for a firm's work and clients. Self-reported scale: 40K+ accounting professionals across 34 countries, 5.5M jobs completed by customers in 2024; #1 on G2 for practice management for 19 consecutive quarters.
category: Vertical SaaS — accounting practice management / professional-services work OS (AI layered on top, not AI-native)
stage: Late-stage growth (post-Series B). AFR reported a $93M raise in Feb 2022 at a ~$402M valuation; an earlier $7M round in 2018.
funding: ~$100M+ disclosed. $7M (June 2018, per AFR); $93M raise announced Feb 2022 valuing the company at ~$402M (AFR / Startup Daily). Specific lead investors could not be confirmed from accessible sources — do not treat any investor name as verified. Karbon's own site says only that it is 'well-funded'.
headcount_estimate: 201-500 (LinkedIn company page band; ~451 employee profiles listed). Offices in the US, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, the UK and the Philippines.
yc_or_accelerator: None found — no YC or accelerator affiliation surfaced
sells_to: B2B SMB and mid-market — accounting firms from small practices up to large multi-partner firms; sold via demo/sales-led motion
how_they_use_agents: Two layers. (1) In-product: 'Kai', an AI coworker positioned as grounded in firm-specific data — the marketing line is 'Kai knows your clients, your work, and your team.' It answers questions and executes tasks against live firm data (clients, work history, team, communication records, jobs, capacity, time tracking, budgets, billing, payments). Karbon also markets AI email triage/summarization, automated period-close, and, listed as 'Coming Soon', AI Agents that 'proactively handle repetitive workflows like client onboarding and tax preparation.' (2) Internally: they are a Slite customer — Simon Hilton, Director of Product, gave the testimonial. So the company both builds a context-grounded agent and buys an internal knowledge/agent-memory tool.
why_they_need_memory: Karbon's own product pitch is essentially an argument for agent memory: 'The longer you're on Karbon, the more it knows and the more it can do for you' — they explicitly differentiate Kai from generic AI on the grounds that it does not start from scratch each interaction. Agents that run client onboarding or tax prep must carry durable per-client, per-engagement state across multi-year cycles and staff turnover, which is exactly a long-horizon memory problem. Separately, as a 200-500 person company distributed across six countries, their internal buying reason (the Slite use case) is a queryable company brain so product and ops knowledge survives distance and headcount growth.

name: Displayce
what_it_does: Programmatic Digital Out-of-Home (DOOH) adtech. Displayce sells a demand-side platform (DSP) for planning, buying and real-time optimization of DOOH campaigns across 2M+ premium screens in 80 countries, plus a DMP for centralizing and enriching OOH asset data, dynamic creative optimization (DCO), and context-based targeting (geo-behavioural, retail, flight-based). Three buyer types: brands and media agencies, media owners monetizing their screen inventory, and adtech partners who integrate the DOOH stack via API. Claims 800 brands served; named clients/partners include JCDecaux, Havas, Jellyfish, Kinesso, OUTFRONT, Decathlon and Uber.
category: Adtech — programmatic DOOH DSP/DMP
stage: Acquired / corporate-owned. Bootstrapped-to-small-seed early on, then majority stake taken by strategic acquirer JCDecaux in July 2022. Not venture-stage today.
funding: €850,000 raised in 2016 (per company site). JCDecaux acquired a majority stake in July 2022; transaction value not disclosed. No later venture rounds found.
headcount_estimate: 51-200 (LinkedIn band). Company site notes 23 hires in 2023 and 9 offices — Bordeaux (HQ), Paris, Brussels, London, Madrid, Milan, São Paulo, Dubai, Berlin. Realistically ~80-150.
yc_or_accelerator: None found — French company, no YC or named accelerator surfaced
sells_to: B2B enterprise — brands, global media agencies and media owners; plus a developer/partner channel via API integration
how_they_use_agents: Weak on the product side, clear on the internal side. In-product 'AI' is optimization/ML rather than LLM agents: AI-assisted media planning, activation and bid/media optimization with granular contextual targeting, plus dynamic creative optimization. No LLM agent product is marketed. The agent-memory purchase is internal ops: Claire Villet, Operations Manager, is the Slite reference — she describes Slite's 'Ask' AI agent as having 'simplified information gathering for the whole team' and eliminated recurring 'How does X work' / 'Where can I find Y' messages. So Displayce is an internal-knowledge buyer, not an agent-product builder.
why_they_need_memory: Ops-heavy, geographically fragmented business: ~100 people spread across nine offices in Europe, LATAM and MENA, working in multiple languages, running campaign operations against inventory rules that differ by country and media owner. Institutional process knowledge lives in people's heads and Slack, and the named pain was repetitive question-answering across the team. That is the classic 'company brain' buyer profile: distributed ops team, high process surface area, no dedicated internal-comms function. Their memory need is organizational, not per-user agent state.

name: JobTarget
what_it_does: Recruitment-marketing and job-distribution platform. Core value prop is 'post once, reach everywhere': distribute a job to 25,000+ job boards from one dashboard, plus programmatic job advertising with automatic budget reallocation across 100+ partner sites. Around that sits a wider suite — JobTarget 360 (unified platform), Candidate Manager (lightweight applicant tracking), Sourcer against 90-120M passive candidate profiles, Easy Apply, automated video screening, a Compensation Analyzer, JobTarget Intelligence analytics, and automated OFCCP federal-contractor compliance. Deep ATS-integration surface. Self-reported: 10,000+ businesses, 200M+ job postings, 1B+ applications; named customers include Peet's Coffee, Dow Jones and NYU.
category: HR tech / recruitment advertising, job distribution and compliance
stage: Bootstrapped and independent. The company states plainly that it has 'no outside investors' and is not answerable to external shareholders. ~25 years old, so a mature private operating business rather than a startup.
funding: None disclosed. Company explicitly describes itself as independent with no outside investors. No venture rounds, no acquisition found.
headcount_estimate: 51-200 (LinkedIn band). Remote-first; registered HQ 600 Summer St, Stamford, Connecticut.
yc_or_accelerator: None — bootstrapped, founded 2001, predates the modern accelerator era
sells_to: B2B, broad band — 'lean recruitment teams to Fortune 500 companies'; also a partner/integration channel with ATS vendors and job boards
how_they_use_agents: Product-side AI is feature-level rather than agentic: an AI Job Description Builder that generates and customizes postings, a Compensation Analyzer doing market-data salary benchmarking, programmatic distribution that automatically adjusts spend to optimize results, and automated video screening. No autonomous LLM agent product is marketed. The agent-memory purchase is internal and engineering-led: Donald Sipe, Principal Engineer, is the Slite reference and describes migrating the company off Confluence specifically so the entire company — not just the product team — writes and organizes content in one place that the AI can answer from.
why_they_need_memory: A 25-year-old, remote-first company whose actual product is an enormous integration and rules surface: 25,000+ job boards each with its own posting quirks, 100+ programmatic partners, ATS integrations, and OFCCP compliance rules that change with federal directives. That accumulated operational knowledge is the moat, and it is exactly the kind of thing that decays in a wiki. Their stated buying trigger was adoption breadth — Confluence was a product-team tool, and they wanted a knowledge base the whole company would actually write into so it could be queried. For an agent-memory vendor this is the 'legacy institutional knowledge, long tenure, remote workforce' profile rather than the 'AI-native startup needs agent state' profile.

name: Tset (Tset Software GmbH)
what_it_does: Vienna-based B2B vertical SaaS for product cost engineering and product carbon footprinting in discrete manufacturing. Its platform, Tset Studio, does automated bottom-up 'should-cost' calculation and CO2 emissions estimation for parts, tools and assemblies, spanning design-to-cost, sourcing/supplier negotiation, quoting and project profitability. It extracts 2D/3D CAD geometry and applies cost models plus ML to produce detailed cost and carbon breakdowns from limited input, claimed ~10x faster than manual costing. Named customers: BMW Group, Bosch Rexroth, Brose, ZF, AGCO, Lego, Thyssenkrupp, Draeger, KTM, TE Connectivity, Stabilus, Chiron Group, Kuester. Offices in Vienna (HQ, Aspernbrueckengasse 2) and Kuchl, Austria.
category: Industrial vertical SaaS — manufacturing cost engineering / should-cost + carbon accounting
stage: Series A (July 2024); now being acquired — A2MAC1 signed a binding agreement to acquire Tset on 18 June 2026, expected to close Q3 2026
funding: ~EUR 35M disclosed across rounds, though rounds may partially overlap: pre-seed 2021; EUR 9.6M seed 2022; ~EUR 13M round March 2023 (Brose Ventures, ZF, impact investor Alois Flatz); EUR 12.7M Series A July 2024 (Carbon Removal Partners, Brose Ventures, Ingenics Holding). Dealroom buckets total funding at $10–50M. Exact cumulative total not confirmed.
headcount_estimate: ~100–150. Own press release said 70 employees (March 2023) and 'more than 100 developers and industry experts' across Vienna and Kuchl (July 2024); LinkedIn lists 51–200; Dealroom says <100.
yc_or_accelerator: None found — no YC or accelerator affiliation surfaced. Strategic/corporate VC backed instead (Brose Ventures, ZF, Ingenics).
founded_year: 2018 (founded in Vienna by Andreas Tsetinis and Sasan Hashemi; Dealroom lists founding activity from 2017 with the entity established 2018)
sells_to: B2B enterprise — automotive OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers, aerospace, machinery/equipment, electronics and industrial manufacturers. Long enterprise sales cycles, procurement/cost-engineering/R&D buyers.
how_they_use_agents: No AI agents in the product, and the word 'agent' does not appear anywhere on the site. The automation is deterministic cost simulation plus machine learning: 2D/3D CAD data extraction, ML models that automate bottom-up cost calculation, and 'automate part, tool and supplier costing.' LinkedIn specialties do list machine learning, data science and artificial intelligence, and acquirer A2MAC1 frames the deal as building 'AI-enabled Costing Intelligence,' combining its benchmarking data and 'advanced AI capabilities' with Tset's simulation engine — so AI is a roadmap/positioning theme, not a shipped agent. Their Slite usage is purely internal knowledge management, not agent memory.
why_they_need_memory: A 100+ person, domain-dense engineering org across two Austrian sites, encoding highly specialized institutional knowledge: manufacturing process logic, per-customer calculation methodologies, cost driver models, CO2/CBAM regulatory rules. That knowledge accumulates as documentation faster than it can be curated. The testimonial from Roman Kuba (VP Engineering) is explicitly about corpus maintenance at scale — bulk actions to avoid reviewing every doc manually — i.e. the pain is doc sprawl and staleness in an engineering wiki. The June 2026 A2MAC1 acquisition raises the stakes further, since post-merger integration makes captured institutional knowledge load-bearing.

name: Enteractive
url: https://enteractive.com (NOTE: the cited URL https://enteractive.eu is now a parked/lander domain and no longer serves the company site — the live site moved to enteractive.com)
what_it_does: Malta-headquartered outsourced player reactivation and retention provider for online gambling (iGaming) operators. Human sales agents place 1:1 outbound phone calls, in the player's own language, to reactivate dormant/lapsed accounts and convert unfunded registrations, on a pay-only-when-players-play performance model. Delivered through a proprietary platform, (Re)Activation Cloud (launched 2017), which connects via secure API to an operator's inactive player database, plus a Dialer system and a Client Dashboard for campaign monitoring. Claims for 2025: 15M+ players called annually, 1M+ players called in a single month, 1M+ cumulative reactivations, and EUR 75M added operator NGR. Clients/partners named on site: Betsson Group, Kindred Group, Stake, NetBet, Coolbet, Rootz, Rhino Entertainment, plus CRM platform partnerships with Optimove and FastTrack. Malta HQ (Gzira) and a US office in Fort Lauderdale, Florida (opened Jan 2023). G4 responsible-gaming accredited and Cyber Essentials certified.
category: iGaming CRM/retention — outsourced outbound player engagement (BPO + proprietary SaaS platform)
stage: Private, mature (18 years old); growth-equity backed rather than classic VC-staged. Bettor Capital made a growth investment in May 2024 to strengthen North American expansion.
funding: Unknown / undisclosed. The only financing event disclosed publicly is a May 2024 investment from Bettor Capital (amount not stated). No seed/Series A/B rounds surfaced — the company grew largely on services revenue since 2008.
headcount_estimate: ~250. Their Teamtailor careers site counters read 2 offices, 40 nationalities, 250 colleagues. Actively hiring bilingual Reactivation Sales Agents plus an in-house Tech team (Python developer, full-stack developer, Azure/DevOps cloud engineer) in Malta.
yc_or_accelerator: None — not an accelerator company. Founded 2008, long predates the relevant accelerator cohorts.
founded_year: 2008 (founded in Stockholm by Mikael Hansson and Bo Sehlstedt; relocated operations to Malta, moving to a Sliema office in 2010, now Gzira)
sells_to: B2B enterprise — online casino and sports-betting operators, including large multi-brand groups (Betsson, Kindred, Stake). Sold to CRM/retention and commercial leadership at operators, in 50+ regulated markets.
how_they_use_agents: Important disambiguation: 'agent' at Enteractive means a human Reactivation Sales Agent, not an AI agent. Their homepage positioning is explicitly anti-automation — 'No robocalls. Real people. Having one-to-one conversations' — and client testimonials sell them precisely as the channel that works on players who ignored 'automated CRM tools.' AI does appear, but narrowly: the (Re)Activation Cloud page says they 'combine advanced technology and AI analytics with personal interaction,' i.e. AI is used for player segmentation, propensity scoring and risk-gambling behaviour monitoring that routes which human calls whom. There is no AI voice agent and no agent-memory use case in their product.
why_they_need_memory: ~250 employees, 40 nationalities, two offices on two continents, running a high-turnover multilingual call floor. Every campaign has operator-specific scripts, offers, and market-by-market regulatory and responsible-gambling constraints (G4 accreditation, data protection, 50+ jurisdictions), and new bilingual agents must be onboarded and made productive fast. That is a classic internal enablement/knowledge-base problem: many people, high churn, content that must be current and findable in the moment. Notably, the Slite testimonial comes from a Project & Change Manager and is about vendor support responsiveness during rollout — a change-management/enablement buyer, not a product or AI buyer.

name: Wecasa
what_it_does: French consumer marketplace and mobile app for booking at-home services, tagline 'Sponsor officiel de la vraie vie.' Six verticals: house cleaning and ironing, childcare/babysitting, at-home hairdressing, beauty/esthetics (manicure, waxing, semi-permanent polish), massage, and personal training/yoga/pilates. Customers book a vetted independent professional to come to their home; Wecasa handles matching, scheduling, payment collection, invoicing and after-sales, and supports the French service-a-la-personne tax credit and CAF/CMG childcare subsidies. Supply side runs on a separate Wecasa Pro app where independent pros set their coverage area, hours and services and accept pushed job proposals. Scale: ~10,000 partner independent professionals across France, ~300,000 clients, 1.5M+ services delivered, 4.9/5 rating. HQ at 46/48 rue Rene Clair, Paris 18e. International sites live for the UK (wecasa.co.uk), Germany (wecasa.de) and Austria (wecasa.at), with expansion to UK/Germany/Austria/Switzerland dated from 2024.
category: Consumer home-services marketplace (gig/local services, B2C two-sided platform)
stage: Series B+ / growth stage. Dealroom records Seed, Series A, and a Series B+ round led by iXO Private Equity.
funding: Total $10–50M per Dealroom's bucketed estimate; exact cumulative total not confirmed. Confirmed data point: EUR 4.5M raised end of July 2019 (reported by Le Monde). Investors by round per Dealroom — Seed: ISAI Gestion, Pierre Kosciusko-Morizet, Yvan Wibaux, Sebastien Forest; Series A: Serena, Kernel Investissements, Frederic Mazzella (BlaBlaCar founder), Blisce; Series B+: iXO Private Equity. Idinvest publicly flagged Wecasa as a beauty-sector 'rising star' in 2020.
headcount_estimate: ~80–150 internal employees. Their own 'qui-sommes-nous' page states 80 people based in Paris 18e (figure written as of 2023); LinkedIn lists 51–200; Dealroom estimates 100–500. Separately ~10,000 partner professionals, who are independent contractors, not employees — do not conflate these.
yc_or_accelerator: None found. French VC-backed (ISAI, Serena, Blisce, iXO), no accelerator affiliation surfaced.
founded_year: 2016 — company press page says created September 2016 by 5 co-founders; Le Monde reported 2017, which appears to be a later reference point. Co-founders named in press: Julien Lestavel and Antoine Chatelain (both Centrale engineers) and Pierre Andre (business school), the last of whom is the Slite testimonial author.
sells_to: Prosumer / B2C — individual consumers in French (and now UK/DE/AT/CH) cities, primarily busy urban professionals and families. Secondary supply-side acquisition targeting independent service professionals.
how_they_use_agents: No AI agents anywhere in the product, and no AI messaging on the site at all. The only automation is algorithmic dispatch: customer bookings are matched and pushed as proposals to nearby qualified pros via the Wecasa Pro app, which pros accept or decline. There is no LLM, chatbot, or agentic layer surfaced publicly. This company is a pure internal-knowledge-management buyer, with zero AI-product connection to the vendor category.
why_they_need_memory: An ~80–150 person HQ team supports a 10,000-pro supply network and ~300,000 customers across six service verticals and four to five countries. Operational knowledge multiplies combinatorially — per vertical, per country, per regulation (crédit d'impôt, CAF/CMG childcare rules, pro vetting and diploma requirements, hygiene protocols) — and both customer support and pro support need the right answer in seconds. Their testimonial is the single clearest statement of the buying trigger across all three companies: they had already built an internal knowledge base, but its search did not work, so nobody could find anything and adoption collapsed. That is precisely the retrieval-quality failure that pushes a non-AI company to buy an AI-search 'company brain' — the pain is findability, not agents.

name: Agorapulse
what_it_does: Social media management SaaS. One dashboard to publish/schedule across Facebook, Instagram, X, LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky, Reddit and Google Business Profile; a unified social inbox for comments/DMs with moderation; social listening; reporting; and a 'Social ROI' module that attributes sales, leads and traffic to organic posts. Subscription tiers from a free plan (1 user, 3 profiles) up to agency/enterprise. Verified scale: ~31K social media managers and 3,000+ agencies claimed on site; French registry shows €14.76M revenue and €1.39M net income for FY2021 (SIREN 432322964).
category: social media management SaaS / martech (B2B SMB + agency)
stage: Growth-stage private, profitable. Bootstrapped until a single 2019 growth round; no later round found.
funding: €16.6M growth investment announced 18 Sept 2019 from Hi Inov Dentressangle, Cipio Partners and Entrepreneur Venture; previously bootstrapped. No subsequent round found in press or registry filings. Dealroom shows a $10–50M total-funding band and a $25–100M revenue band (ranges only, unverified).
headcount_estimate: ~160 employees. Slite's case study states 160, hybrid, with staff in 12–13 countries; French INSEE employee band for the entity is code 22 = 100–199 salaried (2023 reference year).
yc_or_accelerator: None found — not a YC or accelerator company; bootstrapped from 2011 to 2019.
founded_year: 2011 (Agorapulse founded in Paris by Emeric Ernoult and Benoit Hédiard; note the underlying French legal entity SIREN 432322964 was registered 2000-07-15, a predecessor vehicle, and Dealroom lists 2010)
sells_to: B2B SMB and mid-market plus digital agencies (3,000+ agencies); verticalized pages for e-commerce, B2B, manufacturing, retail and higher education. Buyer is the social media manager / head of social.
how_they_use_agents: In-product, deliberately assistive rather than agentic — the AI page states outright: 'Our Assistants, not agents, are dedicated to collaborating with you,' keeping a human in the loop. Shipped features: Writing Assistant, AI reply suggestions with sentiment analysis, hashtag suggestions, alt-text generator, best-time-to-publish, AI report summaries, listening wordcloud. The genuinely agentic surface is outbound: Agorapulse ships a self-hosted MCP server so users can drive their social accounts from inside ChatGPT or Claude. A separate product, 'Archie', an AI content engine that repurposes existing content for social, is in beta/early access. Internally they are heavy agent users: they run Slite's MCP inside Claude for documentation retrieval.
why_they_need_memory: The clearest internal-buyer profile of the three. 160 people across 12–13 countries with no single office; migrated off Tettra + scattered Google Docs to a single documentation repository (rejected Notion as too complex). They use Slite's MCP server in Claude and Slite AI search across Slack, Drive and more, and cite a 10x drop in the number of questions people ask colleagues because retrieval now works. AI is a named function, not a side project — Alexis Dupont's title is Director of AI Transformation. Concrete retrieval jobs cited: when a feature shipped, why past decisions were made, and competitive intelligence for sales/CS ('why do we win versus Hootsuite?'). That is exactly the 'company brain' use case: cross-tool, cross-timezone institutional recall feeding an LLM.

name: Premium Plus
what_it_does: Not a software vendor — a European Zendesk implementation and optimisation consultancy, and Zendesk's top EMEA partner (self-described 'EMEA Zendesk Partner of the Year'). Service lines: Zendesk implementation, data migration, licensing (they resell), training, health checks, optimisation, analytics, AI & automation, plus built add-ons — AI agents, Copilot enablement, voice solutions, custom themes, apps/integrations, a P+ Self-Service Portal, and a 'Premium Care' retainer. Claims 1,000+ projects delivered, 15+ years of Zendesk expertise, NPS 9.2. Belgian BV, enterprise number BE 0844.776.562, registered 28 March 2012.
category: CX/EX consultancy and Zendesk implementation partner; services + AI-agent deployment (not a product company)
stage: Bootstrapped / privately held owner-operated services firm. No venture funding found in any source; Belgian registry shows a private limited company with individual directors, not an investor cap table.
funding: Unknown — none found. No VC, PE or accelerator funding appears in press, Dealroom or the Belgian Crossroads Bank for Enterprises record. Almost certainly self-funded from services and Zendesk licensing revenue, but treat the absence as unconfirmed rather than proven.
headcount_estimate: ~30 employees (stated on their own About Us page), across offices in Sint-Niklaas (HQ, Belgium), Lille (France) and London (UK), plus remote staff. Slite's case study says 93% of the company uses Slite.
yc_or_accelerator: None found — a Belgian consultancy, not an accelerator-backed startup.
founded_year: 2012 (Belgian CBE start date 28 March 2012; the company markets '15+ years of Zendesk expertise', which likely counts founders' experience predating the entity)
sells_to: B2B mid-market — European companies of roughly 100–1,500 employees, concentrated in retail/e-commerce, financial services and technology/SaaS. Buyers are CX and EX leaders (support/service directors), not developers.
how_they_use_agents: Agents are the product they sell to clients, not something inside their own SaaS. They design and deploy Zendesk AI agents described as 'autonomous bots that answer customer questions without human involvement,' running 24/7 off the client's knowledge base. Their stated methodology is content-first: knowledge-base content audit and restructuring, intent mapping (what AI can safely handle vs. what needs a human), answer templates, escalation logic, integration to order systems/CRM/billing for real-time lookups, then resolution-rate and CSAT tracking. Timelines 6–8 weeks for a pilot, 12–16 weeks for full rollout, with most of that time on content prep rather than configuration. They publish honest deflection expectations: 60–80% for simple lookups, 20–40% for complex troubleshooting, 30–50% overall. They also deploy Zendesk Copilot for agent-assist and voice AI.
why_they_need_memory: Two reinforcing reasons, which is what makes them an unusually good ICP for this category. (1) Their entire consulting thesis is that agents are only as good as the knowledge behind them — their AI-agents page says explicitly that agents need 'clean documentation, structured answers', and most of a deployment is content work. A firm that bills for structuring knowledge so agents can retrieve it is a natural buyer of tooling that does the same. (2) Internally, ~30 people spread over three countries had documentation scattered across platforms; they evaluated Notion vs. Slite on mobile access, integrations, collaboration, document management, flexibility and security, chose Slite for adoption, seeded it with a company handbook, assigned per-area channel admins to keep content fresh, and rely on AI search to cut interruptions for routine questions. They also integrate it with Asana.
sources: https://kbopub.economie.fgov.be/kbopub/toonondernemingps.html?lang=en&ondernemingsnummer=0844776562 (Belgian CBE: PREMIUM PLUS, start date 28 March 2012, private limited company, Grote Markt 6A 9100 Sint-Niklaas; permanent representatives Thomas D'Hoe, Kristof Bartok, Kurt Pinoy)

name: wundertax
what_it_does: German consumer tax-filing software (DIY taxtech). A guided web/app flow that lets a private individual complete and submit a German income tax return in a claimed ~17 minutes, with live refund calculation as you type, automated plausibility checks, and electronic submission to the tax office over the official ELSTER interface — no tax knowledge required. Freemium pricing: build the return for free, pay only when you file. Sold through segment-specific funnels (employees, self-employed, students, expats, police, military, pensioners), a legacy of its origins as a student tax product. Claims 1M+ customers and over €1B in refunds obtained; 4.8 stars on Google, German hosting, and a 'Top Steuer-App' award.
category: consumer taxtech / fintech (B2C SaaS, transactional)
stage: Series A-stage, no round since 2017. Registry shows repeated share-capital increases (€500 → €25,000 → €33,113 → €45,407 → €54,880) and around 20 known active shareholders, consistent with angel plus VC ownership; the company has been quiet in the press since 2017.
funding: €4M round led by London VC PROfounders Capital, announced December 2017, raised to expand internationally. No later round, exit or acquisition found in press, Google News, Dealroom or the German commercial register. Total raised beyond that €4M is unknown — do not treat €4M as a confirmed lifetime total.
headcount_estimate: Unknown. No public figure found: no team page, no headcount claim on the site, the Personio-powered jobs page currently lists zero open positions, and the North Data financial/employee fields for wundertax GmbH are behind a paywall. Likely small (tens), but that is an inference, not a source.
yc_or_accelerator: None found — not YC; backed by a London seed/Series A VC (PROfounders Capital) rather than an accelerator.
founded_year: 2015 (entity registered 23 Nov 2015 as 'study clever UG', converted to study clever GmbH in March 2016 and renamed wundertax GmbH in May 2017; the site markets '11+ years of experience with tax returns', which points to a 2014-era product start before incorporation)
sells_to: B2C / consumer — German taxpayers filing their own returns, with heavy SEO acquisition via a large tax-advice content library (ratgeber-steuern). Not B2B, not developers.
how_they_use_agents: None visible. Nothing on the German or English site mentions AI, KI, machine learning or agents anywhere in the product — the pitch is a deterministic guided questionnaire plus plausibility checks and an ELSTER submission pipe. Their appearance in this dataset is purely as an internal knowledge-management customer, not because they build or ship agents. This is the weakest agent-adjacency of the three companies.
why_they_need_memory: Internal only, and framed around onboarding rather than agents: they are cited alongside a '75% faster team onboarding' stat, with the CEO emphasising that everyone adopted the tool quickly and uses it actively. The plausible underlying driver is that German tax rules change annually (their own content library tracks Steueränderungen 2024/2025/2026), so process and domain documentation goes stale fast and support staff need current answers during the compressed filing season. That is a wiki/knowledge-base need with an AI-search layer on top — genuine, but a weaker signal for agent-memory infrastructure specifically than either Agorapulse or Premium Plus.
